### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**9** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **68** of **251** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **1** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9abc732132a2f723627d585b049e2cc10869db19` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `54a1b42b0d9830d60758381ecf978b8b6485d29d` — the merge of head `8eb5896ba5786b2c104de77c70291760f5608875` into base `9abc732132a2f723627d585b049e2cc10869db19`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 54a1b42b0d9830d60758381ecf978b8b6485d29d && git checkout 54a1b42b0d9830d60758381ecf978b8b6485d29d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9abc732132a2f723627d585b049e2cc10869db19 8eb5896ba5786b2c104de77c70291760f5608875 && git checkout -B drift-repro 9abc732132a2f723627d585b049e2cc10869db19 && git merge --no-ff 8eb5896ba5786b2c104de77c70291760f5608875

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9abc732132a2f723627d585b049e2cc10869db19
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `8eb5896ba5786b2c104de77c70291760f5608875`
Local-runs: none

Face: declaration (`Clause-②: yes (widening)` on the PR body and changeset; no `packages/spec/src` path, no governed path; l2-review#4 returned it to the lane). Read: the diff at this head, card #36206 with ruling 7077801044, and the head's check-runs.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Additive only.** `OperationSchema.via` is `.optional()`. `PersonaGrantNeed.routedVia` is an output field that only `personaGrantNeeds` fills. In `gradePersonaGrants`, `designedRoutes` returns a route set only when the verb is withheld and not `read`. The new not-measured branch fires only when some route carries a `via`. With no `via` anywhere, `routes[0].confirm` reproduces the old `onlyAwaiting` + `confirmGatedRoutes` result exactly: a defined route set with no `via` means every operation is `pending_confirmation`, and every one carries the same confirm list. The test pins hold this: without `via` the shipped card stays measured and fails; a set that grants the verb still passes; the build missing the named action is measured and fails.
- **All-operations bar in `designedRoutes`: correct, keep.** A partial route set would let one routed write excuse an unrouted write of the same persona × object × verb. That write must hold the grant, so the check has to stay measured. The `MIXED` case (`start_qa_again`) pins it: measured, fails.
- **Loader refusal of `via` on a `refused` write: keep.** Grading never reads `via` on a refused operation (`personaGrantNeeds` records `routedVia` only on applied or pending writes). Accepting the key there would let an author state a route that nothing honours. It is a narrowing of what the loader accepts only for a key this same PR introduces, so nothing already authored can trip it. The refusal row pins it.
- **`via` bound to `run.agentActions` on the operation's object.** The loader enforces it, and two refusal rows pin it (an undeclared action; the card's action on another object). The grader also requires the build to declare the action (`buildDeclaresAction`), so a card-side `via` alone never removes a check.
- **Ruled scope.** The three tagged operations (leave_balances and travel_expense `manager_approves_step_one`; requisition_to_receipt `manager_approves_level_one`) are exactly ruling C plus the travel_expense addition. The library test pins that set. asset_lifecycle `manager_approves_scrap` and order_to_cash `approve_discount` stay untagged with no measured run, as the dispatch order said; the test comment names them.
- **PAY-0044.** 2026-10-01 → 2026-10-02 is the same one-day move as TK-0091 in #36320. The seed `$comment` now states the exception, so the truth can still be worked by hand. West `collected_by_team_last_30_days` 53500 → 58300 is a10's +4800, PAY-0044's amount. The library last-N-days ambiguity pin goes to `[]`. The bank reference follows the date (ACH-1002-058).

### ② Semver level

`patch` for `@objectstack/scenarios`. It is a private, unpublished devx package (CHANGELOG 18.4.0), and its earlier optional-key widenings (`GuardrailSchema.forbids`, `ScenarioCardSchema.workingDays`) shipped as `patch` under the same `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line. AGENTS.md: a changed package takes a `patch` changeset. Correct.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev deviation 1 (Clause-② measured `yes (widening)` against the claim's `no`): accepted. `src/index.ts` re-exports `schema.js` on `.`. Declared on the PR body and the changeset.
- Dev deviation 2 (refused + `via`): kept, see ①.
- Dev deviation 3 (main merged in, closure rebuilt, suite rerun at bb187cac4): fine. The only later commit is the changeset.
- Dev deviation 5 (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:type-check-debt` NOT MEASURED locally, exit 3): CI runs both on this head. The seat's L1 lands only on all-green check-runs.
- Out-of-scope finding (asset_lifecycle / order_to_cash decide-through-action shape): stays on the card as a carrier note, per the ruling. No card is filed.
- open_questions: none.
- SQL push-down: n/a. The diff is grader and loader logic over in-memory card and build facts, with no query path and no id materialisation.
